beginner.confidence: Low–moderate. Wind and showers are improving (NWS discussion 3:08 AM HST), and no NWS watch, warning or advisory is active. But Thursday's island-wide Flash Flood Warning ended only about 4:15 PM yesterday, so today sits inside the ~48-hour runoff flushing period, and the live DOH advisory list could not be read. No buoy data reached. Water color on site decides.
beginner.headline: Today (Fri Oct 9): conditional for beginners, decided by water color. Wind is light SSE (about 5–7 mph) and showers are easing, but Thursday's Flash Flood Warning rain ended less than a day ago, so brown or cloudy water at Waikīkī is likely today, advisory posted or not. Long-period south swell keeps the NWS south-shore forecast at 6–8 ft (exposed breaks, just below advisory); Canoes is far smaller but sets will push.
beginner.recommendation: Treat today's lessons as tentative. Default to reschedule unless, on site, the water at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side is visibly clear, there's no thunder, and several full set cycles look manageable. If it runs, 11 AM–2 PM is preferred: rising tide after the 9:17 AM low, the most flushing time before mid-afternoon, and Surfline expects the leftover wind swell to organize later in the day. One student or a small group of strong adults; multiple students or children only if the water is clearly clean and drift is low. Saturday looks drier with trades returning, but a new long-period south swell arrives then too.
